steps.pre: A triangular flag. Forget formulas: a right-angled triangle is exactly half of a rectangle. The 6 m by 8 m rectangle has area 48 m², so the triangle's area =
steps.say: A triangular flag. No formulas yet, just common sense.

You just used ½ × base × height. That works because the corner is 90°. Tilt the corner and the triangle squashes: its true height shrinks to (side × sinC). So for ANY angle, Area = ½ × a × b × sinC. At 90°, sin90° = 1, and you get ½ base × height back.

steps.pre: Same edges 6 m and 8 m, but now they meet at 30°. Area = ½ × 6 × 8 × sin30°. Since sin30° = 0.5: 24 × 0.5 =

steps.say: That sinC factor is the whole idea. It powers the area formula, the sine rule and the cosine rule, stretching right-angle trig to every triangle. Algebra just labels the sides a, b, c opposite angles A, B, C.

bronze.label: Together: the sine rule for a side
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFind side \(b\) when \(a = 8\), \(A = 30°\), \(B = 90°\). Use the sine rule.

steps.say: Sine rule: \(\frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{a}{\sin A}\), so b = a × sinB ÷ sinA. a = 8, A = 30°, B = 90°, with sin90° = 1 and sin30° = 0.5.

steps.pre: Check the ratios balance: b ÷ sinB = 16 ÷ 1 =

steps.done: Both ratios equal 16, so the sine rule holds. That is the whole move: match each side to its opposite angle, then rearrange.

silver.label: Together: the cosine rule for a side
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFind side \(c\) when \(a = 5\), \(b = 8\), \(C = 60°\). Use the cosine rule.

steps.say: Cosine rule for a side: \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C\). a = 5, b = 8, C = 60°, and cos60° = 0.5.

steps.done: c = 7 cm. New move: the cosine rule finds the third side from two sides and the angle between them.

gold.label: Together: the ambiguous case
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFind the obtuse angle \(B\) when \(a = 9\), \(b = 12\), \(A = 35°\).

steps.say: The ambiguous case. sinB = b × sinA ÷ a = 12 × sin35° ÷ 9. sin35° = 0.5736 (4 d.p.).

steps.done: B = 130.1°. Any sine has TWO angles between 0° and 180°; always ask which one the triangle needs.

bronze.title: Bronze: one formula, straight in
steps: Match each side to the angle opposite it. The sine rule pairs them: b = a sinB ÷ sinA. To find an angle instead, use sinB = b sinA ÷ a and finish with inverse sine.
For an area from two sides and the angle between them: Area = ½ab sinC. Multiply the sides, halve, then times the sine.
Keep sin90° = 1 and sin30° = 0.5 in mind; they turn up a lot.

example.question: Find side b when a = 6, A = 30°, B = 50°.

steps.label: Check
steps.content: B (50°) is bigger than A (30°), so b should be longer than 6

silver.title: Silver: pick the rule and rearrange
steps: Two sides and the angle between them, or all three sides: cosine rule. For a side, \(a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A\), then square root.
For an angle from three sides, \(\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}\), then inverse cosine. Keep the side opposite your angle as the −a² term.
A negative cosine means the angle is obtuse (over 90°), so watch the sign of the top line.

example.question: Find side a when b = 7, c = 10, A = 60°.

steps.label: Check
steps.content: \(a = \sqrt{79}\), which sits between 7 and 10 plus a bit

gold.title: Gold: derive, reverse and adapt
steps: Bearings: the angle between two paths from one point is the difference in bearings. Then reach for the cosine rule.
Backwards from an area: rearrange to sinC = 2 × Area ÷ ab. Three sides but no angle: cosine rule for an angle first, then area = ½ab sinC.
New shapes reuse the same idea: a parallelogram is just two triangles, so its area is ab sinC (no half).

example.question: A parallelogram has sides 6 cm and 10 cm with a 70° angle. Find its area.

steps.label: Check
steps.content: A parallelogram is two triangles, so double it

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelySine rule: \(A = 30°\), \(a = 6\), \(B = 50°\). Find \(b\) to 1 d.p.
bronze.hint: Rearrange the sine rule to b = a times sinB divided by sinA.

guided_steps.say: Sine rule: \(\frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{a}{\sin A}\), so b = a × sinB ÷ sinA. a = 6, A = 30°, B = 50°. sin50° = 0.7660, sin30° = 0.5.

guided_steps.pre: Check the ratios balance: b ÷ sinB = 9.2 ÷ 0.7660 = ?  (to 1 d.p.)
guided_steps.done: and a ÷ sinA = 6 ÷ 0.5 = 12 too, so it holds.

misconceptions.message: The ratio is upside down. b = a × sinB ÷ sinA = 6 × 0.766 ÷ 0.5 ≈ 9.2. Multiplying by sinA and dividing by sinB instead gives about 3.9.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelySine rule: \(a = 10\), \(A = 45°\), \(B = 65°\). Find \(b\) to 1 d.p.
bronze.hint: b = a times sinB divided by sinA.

guided_steps.pre: Sense check: B (65°) is bigger than A (45°), so b should be bigger than a = 10. Enter b again:
guided_steps.done: 12.8 is more than 10, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: The ratio is inverted. b = a × sinB ÷ sinA = 10 × 0.9063 ÷ 0.7071 ≈ 12.8. Dividing the other way gives about 7.8.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelySine rule: \(a = 8\), \(A = 40°\), \(b = 10\). Find angle \(B\) to 1 d.p.
bronze.hint: sinB = b times sinA divided by a, then inverse sine.

guided_steps.say: Sine rule for an angle: sinB = b × sinA ÷ a. a = 8, A = 40°, b = 10. sin40° = 0.6428 (4 d.p.).

misconceptions.message: sinB and a are the wrong way round. sinB = b × sinA ÷ a = 10 × 0.6428 ÷ 8 = 0.804, giving B ≈ 53.5°. Using 8 × sin40° ÷ 10 = 0.514 gives the wrong 30.9°.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelySine rule: \(A = 50°\), \(a = 9\), \(B = 40°\). Find \(b\) to 1 d.p.
bronze.hint: b = a times sinB divided by sinA.

guided_steps.pre: Sense check: B (40°) is smaller than A (50°), so b should be shorter than a = 9. Enter b again:
guided_steps.done: 7.6 is less than 9, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: The ratio is inverted. b = a × sinB ÷ sinA = 9 × 0.6428 ÷ 0.7660 ≈ 7.6. Dividing the other way gives about 10.7.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFind the area of a triangle with sides 5 cm and 8 cm and included angle \(30°\).
bronze.hint: Area is half of the two sides multiplied, times the sine of the angle between them.

guided_steps.say: Area of any triangle = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\). a = 5, b = 8, and the angle between them is C = 30°.

guided_steps.pre: Halve it (the ½ in the formula): 40 ÷ 2 =
Now multiply by sin30°, which is exactly 0.5: 20 × 0.5 =

misconceptions.message: You may have left out the ½. Area is HALF of a × b × sinC: ½ × 5 × 8 × 0.5 = 10, not 20. Dropping the ½ doubles your answer.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelySine rule: \(C = 80°\), \(c = 15\), \(A = 35°\). Find \(a\) to 1 d.p.
bronze.hint: a = c times sinA divided by sinC.

guided_steps.say: Match each side to its opposite angle: a = c × sinA ÷ sinC. c = 15, A = 35°, C = 80°. sin35° = 0.5736, sin80° = 0.9848 (4 d.p.).

guided_steps.pre: Sense check: A (35°) is the smallest angle, so a should be the shortest side (shorter than c = 15). Enter a again:
guided_steps.done: 8.7 is less than 15, so it fits.

misconceptions.message: The ratio is inverted. a = c × sinA ÷ sinC = 15 × 0.5736 ÷ 0.9848 ≈ 8.7. Dividing the other way gives about 25.8.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelySine rule: \(a = 7\), \(A = 35°\), \(b = 9\). Find angle \(B\) to 1 d.p.
bronze.hint: sinB = b times sinA divided by a, then inverse sine.

misconceptions.message: sinB and a are swapped. sinB = b × sinA ÷ a = 9 × 0.5736 ÷ 7 = 0.738, so B ≈ 47.5°. Using 7 × sin35° ÷ 9 = 0.446 gives the wrong 26.5°.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFind the area of a triangle with sides 12 cm and 7 cm and included angle \(90°\).
bronze.hint: Use Area = half times a times b times sinC, with sin90 equal to 1.

guided_steps.say: Area = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\). a = 12, b = 7, C = 90°, and sin90° = 1.

guided_steps.done: Area = 42 cm². A right angle makes sinC = 1, so it is just ½ base × height.

misconceptions.message: You may have left out the ½. Area = ½ × 12 × 7 × sin90° = ½ × 84 × 1 = 42, not 84. Dropping the ½ doubles it.

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyCosine rule: \(b = 7\), \(c = 10\), \(A = 60°\). Find \(a\) to 1 d.p.
silver.hint: a squared = b squared plus c squared minus 2bc times cosA, then square root.

guided_steps.say: Cosine rule for a side: \(a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A\). b = 7, c = 10, A = 60°. cos60° = 0.5, and 2bc = 140.

misconceptions.message: You dropped the −2bc·cosA term. a² = 49 + 100 − 140cos60° = 149 − 70 = 79, so a ≈ 8.9, not √149 ≈ 12.2.

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyCosine rule: \(a = 5\), \(b = 8\), \(c = 9\). Find angle \(A\) to 1 d.p.
silver.hint: cosA = (b squared plus c squared minus a squared) divided by 2bc, then inverse cosine.

guided_steps.say: Cosine rule for an angle: \(\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}\). Side a is opposite A. a = 5, b = 8, c = 9, so 2bc = 144.

misconceptions.message: Keep the side opposite your angle as the −a² term. Here a = 5 is opposite A, so top line = 64 + 81 − 25 = 120 and A ≈ 33.6°. Putting c = 9 as the subtracted square finds the angle opposite 9 instead: 84.3°.

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFind the area of a triangle with sides 11 cm and 14 cm and included angle \(42°\). Give it to 1 d.p.
silver.hint: Half of 11 times 14, then multiply by sin42.

misconceptions.message: That is a × b × sinC without the ½. Halve it: ½ × 11 × 14 × sin42° ≈ 51.5 cm².

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyA triangle has sides 6, 8 and 10. Use the cosine rule to find its largest angle (opposite side 10) to 1 d.p.
silver.hint: The largest angle is opposite the longest side; cosC = (a squared plus b squared minus c squared) over 2ab.

guided_steps.say: The largest angle sits opposite the longest side, 10. Call it C. \(\cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}\) with a = 6, b = 8, c = 10, so 2ab = 96.

guided_steps.hint: The angle whose cosine is 0 is a right angle.

misconceptions.message: That is an angle opposite one of the shorter sides. The largest angle is opposite the longest side (10): cosC = 0, so C = 90°. The angle opposite 6 works out as 36.9°.

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyTwo sides of a triangle are 9 cm and 13 cm with an included angle of \(110°\). Find the third side to 1 d.p.
silver.hint: Third side squared = 9 squared + 13 squared minus 2 times 9 times 13 times cos110, and cos110 is negative.

guided_steps.hint: Subtracting a negative adds it on.

guided_steps.done: x ≈ 18.2 cm. The obtuse angle makes the third side longer than either given side, which fits.

misconceptions.message: Check the sign of cos110°. It is −0.342, so the last term is −80.0 and x² = 250 + 80.0 = 330, giving x ≈ 18.2. Treating cos110° as +0.342 gives x² = 170 and the wrong 13.0 cm.

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyFind the area of a triangle with \(a = 15\), \(b = 20\) and included angle \(C = 75°\). Give it to 1 d.p.
silver.hint: Half of 15 times 20, then multiply by sin75.

misconceptions.message: That is a × b × sinC without the ½. Halve it: ½ × 15 × 20 × sin75° ≈ 144.9 cm².

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyCosine rule: \(a = 4\), \(b = 7\), \(c = 9\). Find angle \(C\) to 1 d.p.
silver.hint: cosC = (a squared plus b squared minus c squared) divided by 2ab, then inverse cosine.

guided_steps.say: Cosine rule for an angle: \(\cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}\). Side c is opposite C. a = 4, b = 7, c = 9, so 2ab = 56.

guided_steps.hint: A negative cosine gives an obtuse angle.
guided_steps.done: C ≈ 106.6°, just over a right angle.

misconceptions.message: Watch the sign of the top line. a² + b² − c² = 16 + 49 − 81 = −16, not +16. A negative cosine means C is obtuse: C ≈ 106.6°. Dropping the minus sign gives the wrong 73.4°.

gold.display: Two ships leave a port. Ship A sails 10 km on a bearing of \(040°\); ship B sails 15 km on a bearing of \(120°\). Find the distance between the two ships to 1 d.p.
gold.hint: The angle between the paths is 120 minus 40; then use the cosine rule.

guided_steps.say: The two paths leave the same port, so the angle between them is the difference in bearings: 120° − 40°. Then use the cosine rule with the two distances.

guided_steps.done: The ships are about 16.5 km apart.

misconceptions.message: You need the cosine rule, not Pythagoras. The angle between the paths is 80°, not 90°, so d² = 325 − 52.1 = 272.9 and d ≈ 16.5 km. Treating it as right-angled gives √325 ≈ 18.0 km.

gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyA triangle has sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. Find its area to the nearest whole number.
gold.hint: Find the angle between two sides with the cosine rule, then use area = half ab sinC.

guided_steps.say: With three sides and no angle, first find the angle between 13 and 14 (opposite 15) using the cosine rule, then use the area formula. \(\cos C = \frac{13^2 + 14^2 - 15^2}{2(13)(14)}\), and 2 × 13 × 14 = 364.

guided_steps.pre: Now area = ½ × 13 × 14 × sin67.4° = 91 × 0.9231 = ?  (nearest whole number)

misconceptions.message: There is no right angle, so ½ × base × height using two sides is wrong. Find an angle first: area = ½ × 13 × 14 × sin67.4° ≈ 84 cm². The value 91 is just ½ × 13 × 14, assuming a right angle.

gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyIn triangle PQR, \(PQ = 8\) cm, \(QR = 11\) cm and angle \(PQR = 100°\). Find \(PR\) to 1 d.p.
gold.hint: PR squared = 8 squared + 11 squared minus 2 times 8 times 11 times cos100, and cos100 is negative.

guided_steps.say: Angle Q is between PQ and QR, so PR is opposite it: \(PR^2 = 8^2 + 11^2 - 2(8)(11)\cos 100°\). cos100° = −0.1736, and 2 × 8 × 11 = 176.

guided_steps.hint: Subtracting a negative adds it on.

misconceptions.message: cos100° is negative (−0.1736), so the last term adds on: PR² = 185 + 30.6 = 215.6 and PR ≈ 14.7. Treating cos100° as positive gives PR² = 154.4 and the wrong 12.4 cm.

gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyA triangle has area 30 cm² and two sides of 10 cm and 8 cm. Find the angle between those two sides to 1 d.p.
gold.hint: Rearrange the area formula: sinC = 2 times area divided by ab, then inverse sine.

guided_steps.say: Work backwards from the area. Area = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\), so sinC = 2 × Area ÷ (a × b). Area = 30, a = 10, b = 8.

misconceptions.message: You may have left out the ½. Area = ½ × a × b × sinC, so sinC = 2 × 30 ÷ 80 = 0.75 and C ≈ 48.6°. Using 30 ÷ 80 = 0.375 (no ½) gives the wrong 22.0°.

gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyA parallelogram has sides 6 cm and 10 cm with an angle of \(70°\) between them. Find its area to 1 d.p.
gold.hint: A parallelogram is two triangles: work out ab times sinC (no half).

guided_steps.say: A parallelogram is two identical triangles. Each triangle is \(\tfrac{1}{2}\times 6\times 10\times\sin 70°\). sin70° = 0.9397 (4 d.p.).

guided_steps.pre: Two triangles make the parallelogram: 28.2 × 2 = ?  (to 1 d.p.)
guided_steps.done: Area ≈ 56.4 cm², the same as a × b × sin70°.

misconceptions.message: That is the area of ONE triangle (½ × 6 × 10 × sin70°). A parallelogram is two of them, so double it: 6 × 10 × sin70° ≈ 56.4 cm².

problem_bank.bronze_description: Use the sine rule for a missing side or angle, or the area formula ½ab sinC with a nice angle.
problem_bank.silver_description: Pick the cosine rule (a side or an angle) or the area formula, then rearrange to the unknown.
problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-step problems: derive an angle from bearings or three sides, work backwards from an area, or adapt the formula to a new shape.

method_card.title: Sine Rule, Cosine Rule & Area Formula
steps: Label sides a, b, c opposite angles A, B, C.
A side with its opposite angle known: sine rule, a ÷ sinA = b ÷ sinB.
Two sides and the angle between them: Area = ½ab sinC, or cosine rule for the third side.
All three sides: cosine rule rearranged gives an angle.
method_card.content:
These tools work in any triangle, not just right-angled ones.

Area = \(\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\) uses two sides and the angle between them.

Sine rule pairs each side with its opposite angle: use it when you know one such pair plus one more side or angle.

Cosine rule covers the rest: two sides and the included angle to find the third side, or all three sides to find an angle. A negative cosine gives an obtuse angle, so check the sign.
